notes: Now published as 'SBI Personal Loan'; the old Xpress Credit URL slug 404s. Rate published as a full range built up transparently: 2-year MCLR 8.75% plus a 1.25%-6.25% spread, effective 10.00%-15.00% p.a., with a Q4 FY25 mean of 12.68%. SBI publishes a real FOIR: EMI/NMI up to 65%, alongside a 30-times-NMI cap. Salaried only, and narrower than most - eligibility is confined to Government, Defence and corporate-sector employees who hold an SBI salary package account. Minimum net monthly salary is Rs 20,000 for Government and Defence employees and Rs 25,000 for corporate-sector employees; the lower figure is recorded here. Processing fee 1.50% + GST with a Rs 1,000 floor and a Rs 15,000 cap, waived entirely for Defence and Platinum/Rhodium salary-package customers and halved for Government employees and for scores of 800+. No minimum CIBIL is published - the page says only 'a decent credit score, as per Bank's internal policy'. SBI's own pages disagree on the ceiling: the product page says Rs 50 lakh while its YONO page says Rs 35 lakh. The only published exclusion is by purpose, not industry - the loan may not fund speculative activity.

Salaried only: HDFC Bank's eligibility page states self-employed applicants are not eligible for this product and directs them to a business loan. Restricted to employees of private limited companies and public sector undertakings, with 2 years' total work experience and 1 year with the current employer. Rack rate published as a genuine range, 9.99%-24.00% for salaried. Processing fee is a flat cap of Rs 6,500 + GST, not a percentage. Published figures conflict across HDFC's own pages: the product page says Rs 25,000-Rs 50 lakh while an eligibility FAQ says up to Rs 40 lakh over 12-60 months, and the rates page publishes no tenure at all. No minimum CIBIL appears in the formal criteria; one FAQ calls 720 'ideal', which is guidance rather than a published floor, so cibilScoreMin is left unpublished. Documents could not be verified - the documents-required page did not respond, and the product page says pre-approved KYC-compliant customers need none.

A score of 750+ is described as preferred rather than required, so cibilScoreMin is left unpublished. Rate published as a true range, 9.99%-16.50%, with an Apr-Jun 2026 actuals table confirming it. Foreclosure 3% of outstanding principal, nil after 24 EMIs paid.

notes: Rate recorded from Axis's formal card-rate build-up: 3-year MCLR 8.90% plus a 0.00%-12.65% spread, fixed with no reset, giving 8.90%-21.55%. Axis publishes two other figures on the same page - loans actually disbursed Apr-Jun 2026 ranged 8.75%-21.55% with a 13.07% mean, while the marketing copy says 9.99% onwards 'to a maximum of 22%'. The card rate is used here because it is the published schedule. Salaried only per Axis's eligibility list (salaried doctors, employees of public and private limited companies, Government and PSU employees); self-employed applicants are not listed and no routing rule is published. Maximum age 60 is measured at loan maturity. Minimum net monthly income is Rs 15,000 for Axis Bank customers and Rs 25,000 for non-customers, though the eligibility page states a flat Rs 15,000 - the lower figure is recorded. No minimum CIBIL is published: 750+ appears only as guidance on what is 'considered healthy'. The eligibility page's '40% of take-home' line is advice to the applicant about existing EMIs, not an Axis FOIR cap, so foirMax is left unpublished. No minimum tenure is published as policy. Processing fee up to 2% + GST on the schedule of charges, though an FAQ on the same page says 1.5%-2%.

notes: Kotak publishes its rate as a single row, 'starting from 10.99% per annum' fixed, with no ceiling anywhere on its rate, fees or FAQ pages - so interestRateMax is genuinely unpublished. Up to Rs 1 crore over 12-72 months. Processing fee up to 5% of the final loan amount plus taxes, non-refundable and deducted at disbursal, so the effective cost can sit well above the headline rate. Salaried only per the eligibility page (employed with an MNC, public limited or private limited company), with a minimum graduation or diploma qualification and 1 year of work experience also published; one FAQ on the documents page suggests self-employed applicants may substitute bank statements or tax details, which contradicts the eligibility table. Kotak's own pages disagree on three fields: age 21-60 in the eligibility tables versus 21-80 in a footer FAQ, CIBIL 750 in the eligibility table versus 685 in an FAQ, and minimum income by account type (Rs 25,000 for Kotak salary-account holders, Rs 30,000 otherwise, Rs 20,000 for Kotak employees) versus by city in a documents-page FAQ. The eligibility criteria table is used for all three. Pre-approved offers need no documentation.

notes: This record is PNB Sahyog Rin, the Personal Loan Scheme for Public, which is the salaried scheme: confirmed Central/State Government or PSU employees with 2 years' service drawing salary through PNB, or others with 3 years' service under a check-off facility. PNB does publish a SEPARATE personal loan scheme for the self-employed on the same page, but it is confined to seven named professions (CA/CS, data analysts, architects and valuers, LIC agents, engineers, software developers, financial consultants), caps at Rs 5 lakh over 60 EMIs, and requires a CIC score of 750+ and gross annual income of Rs 6 lakh - its terms are not the figures in this record. Rate is the published floating grid, banded by CIBIL score and employer: 10.25% for Defence and Para-Military drawing salary through PNB up to 15.10% for corporate and other employees and 15.80% under check-off; the fixed-rate option is 11.25%-16.80%. No minimum CIBIL is published, and deliberately so - the grid prices a 'score less than 681' band. No age band, minimum amount or minimum tenure is published. Processing fee 1.00% (nil for Defence) plus a flat documentation charge of Rs 270 up to Rs 2 lakh or Rs 450 above it. The Rs 15,000 metro/urban take-home floor (Rs 10,000 semi-urban/rural) appears only on PNB's FAQ page, which contradicts the product page on three other fields and looks stale - treat it with caution.

notes: Canara Budget, in two salaried variants: Prime for confirmed Government, Defence, Paramilitary, PSU and autonomous-body employees (up to 25 months' gross salary, maximum Rs 50 lakh), and Delight for confirmed employees of reputed corporates, MNCs, listed companies, institutions, universities, schools, colleges, hospitals and IT/BT companies (maximum Rs 40 lakh). Both require 1 year of service and confirmation in service. Self-employed applicants are not eligible and Canara publishes no unsecured equivalent for them - its other personal loans are secured against deposits or securities. Rate published as a realised range of 9.70%-14.70% (mean 11.86%) and built up as RLLR 8.00% plus a credit-risk premium by internal Credit Risk Grade; note that Budget-Delight applicants graded CRG 4 are published as not eligible at all. foirMax 0.75 is Canara's published rule restated: net take-home pay after all existing and proposed instalments must not fall below 25% of salary or Rs 10,000 per month, whichever is higher - a residual-income floor rather than a conventional FOIR cap. That Rs 10,000 is a post-EMI residual test, NOT an income eligibility threshold, and Canara publishes no minimum salary. No minimum CIBIL is published either: pricing runs off the internal CRG, not a bureau cut-off. Processing fee 0.50% + GST with a Rs 1,000 floor and Rs 5,000 cap, currently discounted 50% under a retail loan festival running to 30.09.2026. No age band, minimum amount or minimum tenure is published.

notes: Published as 'starting from 10.49% p.a.' with no ceiling anywhere - the rate page states the final rate is communicated at approval - so interestRateMax is unpublished. Genuinely open to self-employed applicants: IndusInd publishes three separate eligibility blocks for salaried employees, self-employed professionals and self-employed individuals, rather than routing them to a business loan. Age bands differ by segment: salaried 21-60 at maturity or retirement, whichever is earlier; self-employed 25-65 at maturity - this record carries the union 21-65. Minimum CIBIL 730 is a published requirement. Minimum net monthly income Rs 25,000 applies to salaried applicants; self-employed applicants are instead assessed on a published minimum annual post-tax income of Rs 4.8 lakh. Processing fee up to 3.5%, which the rate page says drops to 1.5%-2% during festive offers. The instant online channel is narrower than the headline: capped at Rs 5 lakh over 48 months, and needs only PAN and Aadhaar numbers with no physical documents.

notes: Branded FIRSTmoney Smart Personal Loan. Published as 'starting from 0.83% per month, equivalent to 9.99% p.a. on reducing balance' with no ceiling, and the bank says the final rate may differ from the advertised one, so interestRateMax is unpublished - the 38% top of its EMI calculator slider is explicitly labelled illustrative and is not a published rate. Open to both salaried and self-employed applicants aged 21-60, Rs 50,000 to Rs 15 lakh over 9-60 months, with a published minimum CIBIL of 710. Processing fee is dynamic, published as 0% to 3.5% inclusive of GST depending on sanctioned amount and profile, with 0% available on select amounts. Documentation is unusually light: no uploads at all, just PAN and Aadhaar numbers with the physical PAN shown during video KYC. The Rs 25,000 minimum salary appears only in the rates-page FAQ and is noted there as varying by applicant and location; the eligibility block itself gives no figure.

notes: Flagship product is FedPremia. Salaried only, and explicitly so: 'personal loans are granted to salaried individuals with minimum monthly salary of Rs 25,000'. Federal also publishes a minimum 3 years in the present job. The canonical rates page publishes 'onwards 11.99%' with no ceiling, so interestRateMax is unpublished; the FedPremia FAQ separately claims a 10.49%-17.99% range, which contradicts the dedicated rates page, and the EMI calculator's 25% and 40-year bounds are generic slider limits rather than product terms. Federal's own pages also disagree on age - 21-55 on the personal-loans eligibility page versus a maximum of 60 at the end of tenure on the FedPremia page - and on tenure, where a FedPremia tile says 48 months against 60 elsewhere; the eligibility page is used here. No minimum loan amount is published, and the 'one to sixty months' phrasing on the product page is marketing copy rather than a stated tenure floor, so tenureMinMonths is left unpublished. No minimum CIBIL is published. Processing/admin fee up to 3%; the CIBIL report charge is nil.

documents: Signed application form with a colour photograph of the applicant
notes: Not an open-market loan: RBL publishes only a PRE-QUALIFIED personal loan for its own existing customers - 'only for existing savings or salary account holders with the RBL Bank'. That relationship gate is the published eligibility criterion, and RBL states no salaried/self-employed split at all, so employmentTypes is left unpublished rather than inferred from the corporate-salary-account route. RBL is the one lender here that publishes a single FLAT rate rather than a range: 18% p.a. fixed, so interestRateMin and interestRateMax are both 18.0. Age 25-55 at onboarding, Rs 30,000 to Rs 5 lakh over 12-36 months, one-time processing fee of 2% deducted at disbursal. Also published: foreclosure 5% of outstanding principal within the first 18 EMIs and 3% thereafter, nil once 12 EMIs are paid without a bounce using own funds, and a late-payment charge of 3% of the EMI + GST. Documentation is minimal for existing account holders - no KYC documents, salary slip or bank statement required. No minimum CIBIL and no minimum income are published.
